title: Aperta: Calibrated, cross-modal accessibility analysis in Python
description: Open-source Python library for cross-modal accessibility analysis on transport networks, calibrated with ground-truth data, with integrated traffic-flow estimation and iterative edge-weight calibration. Path-first routing returns the realized route alongside the travel cost as a single primitive; a tiered origin–destination structure keeps the approach tractable from city to country scale; mode and network are orthogonal, so walking, cycling, and car accessibilities on different networks combine natively. Public-transit travel times computed elsewhere (e.g., with R5 or from a transport model) combine in the same way; native transit routing is planned.
